Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle Monster High toys and accessories are a huge hit with their fan base and the Travel Scaris Convertible vehicle is bound to be a big hit with kids who love Monster High. It is a stylish and attractive toy vehicle with a design that sets it apart from the average kid's toy vehicle.

I'm not usually very impressed with toy vehicles because I have seen so many of them and because most of them look very similar. But this toy vehicle grabbed my attention. The cool, eye- catching, all- around design pattern is one that is bound to warrant a second look and both adults and kids alike will find that it easily stands out against other toy vehicles.

Aside from the exterior, this Monster High vehicle does have other features that make it cool. The stylish wheels glide smoothly across a tile floor or a table without any problem and the vehicle seats up to four Monster High dolls. Rather than have all four dolls face forward, this convertible is a two- seat model with a pair of seats that are actually on top of the trunk, where the dolls face backward. Again, it's something unique that you don't find with other toy vehicles.

The Monster High Travel Scaris Vehicle doesn't have any lights or sounds. This may bother some youngsters, but it is better from an adult perspective because it means no batteries to buy and more imagination required. Most kids will not mind anyway- they will find the vehicle so cool and fun that they will not even notice that it doesn't make noise or have any lights. And another advantage is that boys and girls both seem to like this toy. Girls like it because its Monster High and boys like it because, well, it's a vehicle, which is a toy normally associated with boys.

This Monster High vehicle doesn't have opening side doors, and this is one quality that I wish was different because it would not only look cool, but it would also make it easier to place the dolls into the seats. But other than that, this is a fun, nice- looking toy that belongs in the home of every Monster High fan.
text_fidelity_b: Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set Ok first let me say, we are a "it's Lego or its crap" family. My kids evangelize on the evils of Megablocks and other brands they consider knock offs. But this is such a well engineered and detailed set that my fifteen year old wasn't even grudging when he said, this is a really good set.

And he's right, the detail on this set is super impressive. My son loves it for what seems like very authentic design from a war historian rather than a gamer, so maybe a fan of COD would like it even more.

This is a very challenging build, filled with small parts and unlike Lego that pre bags parts so you can open a single bag to do the first couple pages of instructions, mega blocks has you open 80% of the bags for the first few pages. You end up with an impressive pile of pieces out there. Also unlike Lego, mega blocks will create molded pieces specific to a model so realism can be pushed farther than Lego does. In this set, the body is filled with parts that are not just molded to shape but also in color to seem camouflaged or dirty from use. This truly lends a wonderful realism to the model. We also appreciated that markings are screen printed onto pieces rather than using stickers. Kudos for doing that it makes it feel like a quality set.

I do notice a bit more brittleness in the blocks and brick for brick the quality does not seem to match lego, but I can do little but rave over this set. It is beautiful, it took my son and I working together to get this done in several hours. And once done, this is a beautiful set for display.

Well done Mega Block, you are doing what I thought was impossible, you are winning us over from Lego.

*** additional

My son wanted me to mention that the instructions were hard, I would use challenging. But one thing I did forget, I am partially colorblind and often found it hard to distinguish colors in the instructions if it was not daylight.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set

text_fidelity_a:
MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS The MACTANO Starry Night Building Kit is a micro brick set, so it’s not compatible with regular size building sets. And the bricks really are micro! I don’t recommend this set for kids or anyone with dexterity issues. Many of the pieces are smaller than the tip of a q-tip.

I’ve been building sets for three decades, and I’ll be honest, this one was a big challenge. Patience and attention to detail are extremely necessary. I keep looking at my finished set and noticing mistakes I made, or steps I missed.

The pieces do stay together, very important for an off-brand set. The kit includes a tiny brick separator, it’s cute and much needed.

If I have so much experience, why did I find this set so difficult? First, each step in the instructions is really 2 to 5 steps. For example, step 12 uses over sixty(!) pieces to put together four rows of the backdrop. Every step is like that, and you have to pay extremely close attention to figure out what pieces go where.

Second, sometimes it wasn’t clear what color to use or where a piece should go, but I couldn’t look ahead. Future steps greyed out the colors for previous steps, and sometimes didn’t show the complete build, part of it would be cut off.

Third, some of the colors are very hard to tell apart. I used the wrong shade of blue multiple times, but I quit caring. Most of the painting is blue, so only I know about those mistakes. But for the very dark blue and very dark green, it’s hard to see the outlines of the individual pieces in the instructions.

I build brick sets to relax. Working on this set was the opposite of relaxing for me, since I had to focus so much.
text_fidelity_b: MACTANO The Great Wave Micro Building Blocks Set for Adult Kanagawa Surfs Waves Home Decor Model Toys Building Kit -2296PCS

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Silver There have been a number of games based on the the concept of the Golf card game. Like that game, the point of this game is to have the lowest amount of points in your hand while having a number of blind cards that may be high or low. So you need to replace them while possibly and accidentally passing a great card to the next player in the discard pile. Much like Golf, once you think you have the best hand, you call and end to the game and everyone gets one more round to try to improve them hands. If you are lowest, you get zero points, if you are not, you take a penalty.

So that is the basic idea behind the game, but from there, there are many twists to make the game more interesting. Each card has a secret ability to allow you to see the other card in your village (hand.) Also, there is a mechanism to remove duplicate cards which allows you to quickly dump a lot of points from your hand (village.)

The cards are very nice, the amulet is also nice and allows you to lock a great card so that neither you or others can mess with it. The box could be a lot smaller, basically this is a deck game with a single piece for locking a card. you could put it into a box for a pack of hoyles cards.

All in all, an interesting twist on a classic card game concept.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo Toy This is very cute! Elmo is soft red plush, with big "googly" eyes, a big orange "squeezable" fabric nose, and a bright yellow shirt with a white, plastic-coated star, outlined in blue, with white surround sound waves.

The white star on the shirt shows the spot where you must press a button to "tickle Elmo's tummy" (to activate each sequence) but it is placed just a bit high. To press the center of the button, I have to place my thumb below the star, on the yellow shirt fabric.

My favorite feature is how Elmo's mouth opens and closes while the talking and singing sounds are playing. Incredible engineering and technology went into this toy!

This toy is targeted to ages "2-4 Years." A child has to put one of Elmo's 3 hats on his head for each different play mode. Some 2-year-olds will no doubt have hands large enough to accommodate holding the hats and pushing the plastic tab down into the slot between Elmo's eyes, but some will need assistance.

The toy is packaged in "try me" mode. You can reach through a hole in the front of the box and "tickle Elmo's tummy." When you bring Elmo home, pull the fabric on the bottom to the side, move the switch from "try me" to "on." Then pull the fabric back up and attach with the Velcro strip. Batteries are held firmly in this bottom compartment with a tightly screwed on lid. Requires 4 AA batteries.

4 INTERACTIVE PLAY MODES:

HAT-FREE. I think Elmo is saying, "Hi, hello! Elmo likes to imagine with you, what should we imagine today?" "Place a hat on Elmo's head so we can imagine together." "Let's play together, tickle Elmo's tummy." "Let's play together, squeeze Elmo's nose."
Squeezing Elmo's nose gives different responses, sometimes it's two honks, and sometimes it's a long squeak.

PRINCE ELMO
"Greetings loyal friend, Elmo loves wearing a crown." "Prince Elmo says, bounce Elmo." Elmo has to be "bounced" fairly hard and there is a "boing, boing, boing" sound, followed by, "Squeeze Elmo's nose." After his nose is squeezed, he says, "You did it! Tickle Elmo's tummy." After button on tummy is pushed, he says, "You did it! "Now, first, squeeze Elmo's nose, then bounce Elmo."

If you don't do it right, there's a sound, followed by, "That's not right. First squeeze Elmo's nose, then bounce Elmo."

Elmo asks for three correct actions in a row (squeeze his nose, tickle his tummy, or bounce him). After three correct actions in a row, he'll up the challenge to a two-action sequence.

It's repetitive, with immediate positive or negative feedback.

CAPTAIN COWBOY
"Well howdy partner, hello to Captain Cowboy, yee haa!"
"How many times can you squeeze Elmo's nose?" "Let's bounce together."
Squeeze Elmo's nose and he counts to 20.
Elmo sings a song.

CAPTAIN ELMO
"Squeeze Elmo's tummy to hear a song." Elmo sings a song ("Sailing, sailing over the ocean blue, Captain Elmo loves to listen to all of the sounds, don't you?") and plays a game with sea sounds: a horn, seagull, bell or dolphin. "Squeeze Elmo's tummy when you hear a horn," (or seagull, bell, or dolphin). When Elmo's tummy is squeezed, there is immediate positive feedback: the sound of a xylophone.

This is fun and interactive. Parents can model patience when they show children how to put Elmo's hats on him. Parents can watch their children learn, or play and sing along. Parents can learn about their child's temperament (easy, difficult, slow-to-warm-up) when they see their child's response to Elmo. Some children will be able to play with Elmo by themselves. For some adults, the pitch of his voice and the repetitive sounds could begin to chafe after awhile.

text_fidelity_a:
The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

Happily, the conductor has a hole on the bottom that can be used to tighten or loosen the bolts. My three-year-old niece was content with using this as is and loves the train so much as a toy that I'll give it 3 stars, but I think many children would prefer the fun of the motorized drill. When you press a button, the train makes a chu-chu sound and a very dim white light comes out the front. You can't see the light unless you're looking for it. The "design and drill" is basically some bolts to screw on to hold the covers and the wheels in place. There were several colors of bolts you can choose from to make different "designs."

The engine measures 10 inches long by 6 inches wide by 6 inches tall. The wagon measures 7.5 inches long by 6 inches wide by 3.75 inches tall. The wagon bed is 2 inches deep. The caboose measures 7.5 inches long 6 inches wide and 5 inches tall. Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The wheels roll smoothly and securely, and it is easy to connect the three sections of the train together, so it is a good toy not just a building activity. There are some extra bolts in case some are lost. The train is sturdy and can withstand the rough treatment of a 3-year-old armed with a plastic hammer.

Each part was designed with them in mind. It doesn't magnify much, but it's for the benefit of their eyes. It's also designed so that they don't have to shut one eye to see. It's simple! If you're looking for something more advanced, you'll most definitely want to go another route. This one is more of a toy than a microscope.

It comes with 24 slides, with 3 items on each one. (Plus one blank one.) There's an included book that tells what it is on each of the slides(page 27 and 28). There's no storage for these at all. It would have been nice for a container or bag of some sort to be included to hold all of these. For now, we have the microscope and the slides within a basket, and that makes it easy to pull it off the shelf.

To use the light part of the microscope, you have to put in 2 AAA batteries, which are not included. Flip the switch and a light will come on. Just place a slide under the lens. (It will only go one way.) There's a knob that turns on the front, and this will move the slide back and forth. That's it. There's no way to zoom in and out.

I wouldn't recommend this microscope unless you want it as the most basic introduction to very young children(5ish and under). Even then if they've already been introduced to a microscope, they'll probably be disappointed in this one.

It runs pretty fast on the 6 volt NiCd battery.  It is nearly impossible to roll it over and get it stuck as it just flips over and keeps on going.  Battery life is good (20 to 30 mins).  Controller is a bit small for adult hands but fits my 12 year old granddaughter hands very well.  The car is not DIgitally controlled (its all on or all off- no proportional steering or throttle), but it is able to spin around while staying in place (think tank or dozer like and you get the idea).  Have not had a chance to run it in the water yet as it has been real dry here the last couple weeks.  I tested it on a mowed lawn and gravel driveway and it will handle these surfaces ok.  The plastic tires are getting a little chewed up from the gravel so do be aware that a constant gravel use will probably wear out the tires.  Also tried it on wood and carpet and it runs great on those surfaces.  It comes with a handy phillips screwdriver to take out the 4 (YES 4!) battery cover screws.  I'm guessing so many screws to help keep the battery dry when running in water.  Didn't try out the charging cord as the USB cords are nothing more than a trickle charger and take too long.  I used my B6 V2 chargerer and the battery comes out a little under spec (typical).  Remote takes 2 AA batteries.  Car is fun but there is no suspension and hard plastic tires make for a very stiff drive.  I normally run off road rock crawlers in a dry creek bed so this car really isn't designed for that type of use, but for smooth surface running this is a good fun choice.

I'd like to find one that has a small watch face, bands that can be changed, uses a good app, and can monitor O2, sleep, and a wide variety of exercise. This watch was a perfect 10 in looking nice for my small wrists, and bands that can be changed. Unfortunately it fell quite short of the mark for everything else I needed.

The app has me ready to put this watch back in the box and try something else. It's a really clunky app compared to others I've tried (Fitbit, Da Fit). It's disappointing that there's so few watch faces to choose from. I can't even choose the screen analog look watch face that is displayed on the box, it's not an option on the app at all. The O2 feature is nice, and so is the sleep feature. I do hope they'll continue to work on the app, it does have potential but doesn't work well for me as it is right now.

I'm also having some trouble trying to use the long press on the watch itself to select features. It's just not working no matter how often I try. It's really disappointing that such a beautiful watch has so many problems. I would have really liked to use it as my main watch, but my search will have to continue on.

(Describing which block and where it should go in relationship to the other blocks has been a great skill builder for my group.) My 4 year old, 6 year old, and 7 year old all love playing. My 2 year old likes playing, but he can only play properly by looking at the cards and building what he sees, since he doesn't understand many of the adjectives used in orally describing what to build. AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. For example, the puzzle game would be pretty quick to work except you have to select a piece, use the arrow to move it one square, then select a piece, etc. Lots of clicking the buttons. Still, fun if there aren't other options around.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

Meredith is absolutely beautiful and my daughters love her glamorous clothing and hairstyle. An affordable 18" doll option that doesn't make me cringe to give to impulsive young girls for play.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner I think this thing is awesome!

That said, I do have a couple of warnings to consider. First, it will get really expensive! The sticks don't go very far at all. (The package claims each 6 inch stick will give you 60 inches of play, so I'm going to assume we just need more practice to get that much, as I'm guessing most others will, too.) With this set, you'll get 2 packs of the sticks(48 total sticks...6 each of white, mint green, yellow, orange, blue, red, green, and grey). You'll use those up super quick! These sticks are biodegradable, BPA-free and labeled as "safe". From what I've read, you'll need these specific sticks to go with the 3Doodler.

Also, every time you put a new color stick through the pen, you'll be wasting a bit of the previous stick, unless it works into your design. The whole stick won't completely feed through until you put another one in there to push it on out.

It takes a great deal of practice to get anything worthwhile to turn out. I have 3 little boys and they all want a chance at practicing, so even more sticks are used up in that process. So far, we haven't came up with anything close to what is shown in the practice book, but none of us can call ourselves overly skilled in the artistic realm at this point in time.

All of that said, IF your budget allows for buying lots of sticks to go with this pen, it truly is awesome! (Or you could request packs of these sticks as grandparent presents for the kids.) ;) Letting a child use his/her imagination with this thing is an amazing opportunity, and I definitely recommend it. (I even recommend it for adults, too, because we all need a little childish fun every once in awhile!)

It's easy to use. Just charge it up with the included micro USB cable(or do like me and use your kindle charger), turn it on and wait for the light to turn green. Then, press the button to start it and press it again to stop it. Simple! As I mentioned earlier, there is a book with instructions and some ideas to practice and get started with the pen. There's no worries about getting burned. I tested it out, and while the plastic is a little warm when it first comes out, it's not even close to hot. This allows for a little wiggle room for moving around your design before it completely dries.

In the end, other than the sticks being a costly investment, this is a great little invention, and we've loved it so far!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner

Bendy and the Ink Machine - Boris Buildable Figure (202 pieces), 60 months to 180 months Ok, I do not "lego". I find it equal parts boring and frustrating, that said because I'm a parent I've had to pitch in enough times that I'm "unwilling" but competent. Which is what quickly happened with this set. Granted my kid's only 7, and this is for 14+ (which at this point I agree 100% with). I'm not going to knock a star for that, mine is young and it was a risk he wanted to take. He often does the 14+ lego sets so I figured we'd be fine. NOPE. NO SIR. NOT TODAY.

There were so many tiny pieces, like unnecessarily tiny. He made it to step 2 and couldn't make heads or tails of the instructions. I took a look and also struggled which meant he felt vindicated and took off. So, I spent the next 2 hours debating life choices and contemplating day drinking. Ugh parenting is hard sometimes.

Be very aware: This is not a lego set. The pieces do not snap together as well, or stay together as well, there are no extra pieces, and the instructions are frustrating. I'm keeping my language clean here, but imagine a much more colorful word than frustrating. "Frustrating" really doesn't do the whole experience justice.

However, Boris is built. It can be done. PERSEVERANCE PEOPLE. Kiddo however is not allowed to touch it. It will go up on his bookshelf, like super high and when ever anyone walks in he is to loudly proclaim MY MOM BUILT THAT!

....on the upside it's priced pretty cheap, so if you have any kids in your life whose parents you want to torture, send this to them as a gift. So in the end I'm giving this 3 stars. One star off for the less then stellar pieces, and another star off for the horrendous instructions.

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
Mecha Beasts Playing Cards by Gent Supply I have a few “collectible” decks of playing cards, this one among them. These are fancy cards that are made well and I like them, but the color scheme is a bit off for the black suit cards due to the background.

I’ll start with my main complaint with these first. These are dark cards, using a dark gray background for all suits, and using a dark purple for spades and clubs. This creates a low-contrast scheme that is more difficult to see in low light, and is less than pleasant even in brighter light. This is an unfortunate choice that could have been handled better. A bright purple, or even a strange color choice like orange or blue, would have worked better.

The artwork on these is impressive. A good bit of detail went into each design and it shows. The number cards (2 -10) have small designs on them that are at times hard to see and look at without a magnifying glass, though.

This are well made cards, coated and designed so they will not stick together even in damp climates. They come in a beautiful tuck box with reflective highlights in purple.

Placote - Mission Emotion - Educational Game - Social and Emotional Development - 3 to 7 Years Old My 5 1/2 year old and 3 year old both get a lot out of this game.
The game board is a puzzle and if you lets the kids assemble it, it adds to the length of the game!
Otherwise, playing the game itself usually takes us about 30 minutes as a family of 4.
My 5 1/2 year old like to take the emotion cards and really study them.
She’s entering kindergarten next week and met her teacher this week.
She was pretty shy/nervous.
When we played this game afterward, I made sure to put the card where the kid meets their teacher in the lineup so she would get it! It was perfect because it helped her with understanding her emotions at the time and also helped her know that lots of kids feel that same way!
I like that on the back of the emotions card it shows the emotions they might be feeling - there is a dominant emotion and sometimes a secondary emotion right behind it.
If I had to make any suggestions it would be that the emotion summary sheet it labeled the emotions with the words so you could use those words intended. Sometimes I find myself even using the same words over again but it would be useful even for myself to have a larger emotion vocabulary.
